question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=2x(t)+y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=4x(t)+2y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following gives all equilibrium points of the system of linear differential equations above?
question.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we have

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}]x(t),
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$

The equilibrium (fixed) points of a system ${x}^{′}(t)=f(x,y)$ are the points for which $f(x,y)=0.$ So, we get the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x+y=0 \\ 4x+2y=0\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the second equation is a multiple of the first one:

$$
2(2x+y)=4x+2y,
$$

so we can disregard the second equation.

From the first equation, we get

$$
2x+y=0\,⇒\,y=-2x.
$$

Therefore, the equilibrium points are given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}k \\ -2k\end{aligned}],\,k\in R.
$$
